proposals.before: Shaolian had treated minor matters—the Grand Sacrifices Office's Yi-year name change and the Ministry of Personnel's routine review—as if every office should always attend, listed them in a full memorial, and sought severe punishment, forcing 'severed bureau' officials back into ordinary rows with little distinction among regular posts.
proposals.after: Shaolian had treated minor matters—the Court of Imperial Sacrifices' changes of posthumous names and the Ministry of Personnel's routine review—as if every office should always attend, listed them in a full memorial, and sought severe punishment, forcing 'severed bureau' officials back into ordinary rows with little distinction among regular posts.
proposals.reason: 乙太常易名 means taking Taichang posthumous-name changes as minor; 乙 is 以, not an Yi year.

proposals.before: Shaolian took the minor matter of the Grand Sacrifices Office changing a name in the Yi year and the routine review by the Ministry of Personnel as error, holding that all offices universally should attend the assembly seat, listing it as a full memorial, and burdening it with severe punishment—thus making officials severed from the bureau return to their original rows, dividing regular posts with scarcely any distinction of grade.
proposals.after: Shaolian took the Court of Imperial Sacrifices' changes of posthumous names—a minor matter—and the Ministry of Personnel's routine review, and wrongly held that all offices universally should attend the assembly, listing it as a full memorial and burdening it with severe punishment—thus making officials severed from the bureau return to their original rows, dividing regular posts with scarcely any distinction of grade.
proposals.reason: 乙太常易名 is 以太常易名 (posthumous-name changes), not an Yi-year name change.

decisions.reason: 澶州 is the prefecture Chanzhou; Dazhou invents a different place-name and must be corrected.
The same unit has 澶州; the literal’s Dazhou is the same place-name error, and Chanzhou is the accurate replacement.
王旦為太尉 appoints him Grand Commandant; Grand Preceptor would be 太師 and is a different Three Dukes title.
The literal likewise misreads 太尉 as Grand Preceptor; Grand Commandant matches the Chinese office.
乙太常易名 is 以 plus Taichang’s 易名 (posthumous-name changes), not an Yi-year name change; following 擬諡 confirms the sense.
誤謂 governs the wrong universal-attendance claim; the literal must treat 乙 as 以 and 易名 as posthumous naming, not an Yi-year change.
